newsitem.title: USA: Clinton leads tribute to Ron Brown crash victims.
newsitem.headline: Clinton leads tribute to Ron Brown crash victims.

text.p: President Bill Clinton led an emotional tribute on Thursday to the 35 persons killed one year ago when the aircraft carrying U.S. Commerce Secretary Ron Brown on a trade mission to the Balkans crashed in Croatia.

"Let us resolve always to shine a light of hope and freedom in the darkness, for the people we lost a year ago did not die on a distant mountain because they did not care or did not believe in the possibility of tomorrow being better than today," Clinton said.

"And if we owe them anything at all, we owe them our best efforts to make tomorrow better than today and to spread hope among our people and throughout the world," he told several hundred family and friends of the victims.
Brown's military Boeing 737, with 35 people aboard, crashed on its approach to Dubrovnik airport in Croatia in rain and dense fog. Two of the dead were Croatian.
The trade mission led by Brown included 12 business leaders looking for possible investments that would help the troubled region.

"The people we celebrate today gave their lives building ... worldwide brotherhood for the men and women, the boys and girls alive all over the world, and those yet to come," Clinton said. "It is up to us to celebrate them by continuing that noble work."
Vice President Al Gore also spoke at the memorial service, saying the victims "sacrificed everything in an effort to build a better world."
Miomir Zuzul, Croatia's ambassador to the United States, also sought to comfort the mourners, telling them that those who died "left a permanent mark on the collective soul" of his country.
